slot.brief: Simple trigonometric equation reducible to sin = 0 or cos = 0 form; ask for the general solution set.

stem: The general solution of $\sin 2x=0$, for $x\in\mathbb{R}$, is
working:
$\sin 2x=0\Rightarrow 2x=n\pi,\ n\in\mathbb{Z}$.
Hence $x=\dfrac{n\pi}{2}$. Independent check: \(\sin 2x=0\) implies \(2x=n\pi\), so \(x=\frac{n\pi}{2}\) for \(n\in\mathbb Z\).
solution:
Since $\sin\theta=0$ when $\theta=n\pi$, we have
$$2x=n\pi,\quad n\in\mathbb{Z}.
$$
Hence $x=\dfrac{n\pi}{2}$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$.
